info.title: Akasha API
info.description:
The canon half of the visualizer stack: a store of flat JSON articles with linking, fine-grained sharing and per-article version history.

**Names are addresses.** The triple `database / collection / id` keys every grant, every `[[wikilink]]` and every Chronos `EntityRef`, which is why nothing here renames one. The UI shows a friendlier reading of them (`ember-pact` as "Ember Pact", collections as "categories"); that is presentation only and never reaches this API.

**Deletes are soft.** A deleted article keeps its version history and can be restored; only `DELETE …/collections/{collection}?purge=1` destroys anything for good.

servers.description: Same origin as the akasha service

tags.name: browse
tags.description: Finding your way around: databases, collections, listings and search

tags.name: account
tags.description: Your own profile and collaborator roster

get.description: The only route that needs no session.

post.description: The first account ever registered becomes the administrator. Sends JSON back only when asked for JSON; a browser form gets a redirect. Does not log you in.
One session covers both services: Akasha and Chronos share a `SECRET_KEY`.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

302.description: Redirects to the login page; the cookie is cleared.

get.description: Grant-filtered: a database appears when you can read *something* in it. Reserved (`_`-prefixed) databases are never listed.

delete.summary: Delete a database with no collections left
delete.description: Gated on nothing but being logged in, exactly like creating a namespace: an empty database holds nothing to protect, and emptying it was already owner-only. In practice you will not find one — MongoDB drops a database with its last collection — so this exists for a shell left by an older version.

post.description: Any authenticated user may create a namespace, and owns what they make.

delete.summary: Delete an empty collection you own
delete.description: Refuses while a **live** article remains: emptying a collection is the article endpoint's job. A **tombstone** is the harder case — it holds no article, only the version history of one that was deleted — so it also refuses by default, and goes only with `?purge=1`. Dropping the last collection drops the database with it.

200.description: Dropped; says what went with it.

get.summary: One page of a collection's articles
get.description: `filter` matches every whitespace-separated word against the whole article — slug, title and field values — so it is a full-text search of the collection, not just its names. Ordered by title. An out-of-range `page` is clamped to the last one.
Deletes are soft, so a tombstone still holds the history that makes it recoverable — but nothing else lists it, which would otherwise mean recovery required already knowing the slug you had lost.

200.description: Tombstones and how to undo them.

get.summary: Search one collection by field and text
get.description: `key` finds documents that *have* a top-level field at all; `text` is a case-insensitive substring over the whole body. At least one is required.

post.description: 404 when the namespace does not exist, 409 when a live document already has this id. Creating over a tombstone revives it, keeping its history. The creator owns what they create.

put.description: A full replace, not a merge. `If-Match` is optional but enforced when present: send the rev you read and a concurrent change gives you 409 instead of silently clobbering it. Omitting it is last-write-wins.

delete.description: Soft: the document leaves every listing, search and link, but its version history is kept and it can be restored. Nothing warns you that a Chronos scene may reference it — that shows up in the book's report.

get.description: Answers for a **deleted** document too, which is what makes recovery possible from its own address.
404 when that revision is no longer retained.

post.summary: Restore a version as a new revision
post.description: Never rewinds: the old body is re-applied as the next revision, so the restore is itself in the history. Revives a deleted document. A deletion snapshot cannot be restored (404) — restore the version before it.

get.description: Owner-only. Ownership is holding `delete` at this scope, which the creator gets automatically; the admin role does not confer it.

200.description: Everyone granted at this exact scope.

put.description: Owner-only, and idempotent: re-sharing replaces the role. You cannot share with yourself — it could only reduce your own access.

get.description: Owner-only. Ownership is holding `delete` at this scope, which the creator gets automatically; the admin role does not confer it.

200.description: Everyone granted at this exact scope.

put.description: Owner-only, and idempotent: re-sharing replaces the role. You cannot share with yourself — it could only reduce your own access.

get.description: Across every readable namespace. Scans them all, the same reach `/suggest` has — affordable because it answers a page load, not a keystroke.

get.summary: Link type-ahead over titles and slugs
get.description: Matches slug or title only. An empty `q` returns nothing rather than everything.

post.description: Answers JSON when asked for JSON; a browser form gets a redirect. Rate limited.

sessionCookie.name: session
sessionCookie.description: Signed session cookie from `POST /login` on either service. Akasha and Chronos share one SECRET_KEY, so a single login covers both.

Database.name: database
Database.description: Database (world) name. Names beginning with `_` are reserved and rejected with 400.

DocId.name: doc_id
DocId.description: The article's slug — its permanent address, and what every `[[link]]` and Chronos reference points at.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The revision you based this write on, as an ETag (`"3"`), or `*` for unconditional. Optional, but enforced when present.

Purge.name: purge
Purge.description: Also discard the version history of articles deleted from this collection. Without it, a collection holding tombstones refuses to go.

Filter.name: filter
Filter.description: Every word must appear somewhere in the article — slug, title or any field value.

Page.name: page
Page.description: 1-indexed; clamped into range rather than erroring.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many to return (default 8, capped at 50).

Query.name: q
Query.description: What the writer has typed so far.

ScopeDb.name: db
ScopeDb.description: The database being read, so nearer matches rank first.

ScopeCol.name: col
ScopeCol.description: The collection being read, so nearer matches rank first.

SearchKey.name: key
SearchKey.description: Only documents carrying this top-level field.

SearchText.name: text
SearchText.description: Case-insensitive substring over the whole document.

DocumentWrite.description: A flat JSON object. The id comes from the URL; any `_`-prefixed key is dropped.

Credentials.description: Username and password (email required on register).

RoleWrite.description: The role to grant. Defaults to `editor`.

BadRequest.description: Malformed input: a non-flat document, a reserved name, a bad `If-Match`, or a search with nothing to go on.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but your grants do not cover this.

NotFound.description: No such database, collection, document or retained version.

Conflict.description: Already exists, or the `If-Match` revision is stale, or the namespace is not empty.

ETag.description: The document's current revision, to send back in `If-Match`.

Error.description: Every failure answers with this. Akasha's errors carry a human-readable message and an HTTP status; there is no separate machine code.

Document.description: An article body: a **flat** JSON object. Every value is a scalar or an array of scalars — no nested objects, no arrays of arrays. Enforced on create and update (`validation.py`); a violation is a 400. Two field names are conventional rather than special: `title` becomes the heading and `body` the wikitext prose; everything else renders as an infobox fact.

DocumentResult.description: A document and the revision it is now at. `rev` is also returned as an `ETag`, and is what a later write sends back in `If-Match`.

Identity.description: Who the session belongs to. `must_change_password` is set after an admin reset and until the user changes it.

Registered.description: The first account ever registered becomes the admin; everyone after is a user.

DatabaseSummary.description: `name` is the address; `title` is it rendered readably (`ember-pact` → "Ember Pact", derived, never stored). Counts are of what *this caller* may read.

CollectionSummary.description: `can_write` is permission to create a *new* article here — a grant naming one specific document does not qualify. `can_delete` is ownership.

CollectionList.description: `empty` says the database really holds nothing, as distinct from holding nothing *you* may read — the difference between offering to delete it and telling you to ask for access.

ArticlePreview.description: One row of a browse listing. `updated` and `author` are read off the newest version snapshot, so they cannot drift from the history; both are null for a document written before versioning existed.

ArticlePage.description: One page of a collection, ordered by title. An out-of-range `page` is clamped to the last one rather than erroring. `deleted` counts the tombstones — what a purge would discard, and what could be restored; it is 0 for a caller who could do neither.

RecentList.description: The most recently written articles across every readable namespace, newest first.

DeletedArticle.description: A tombstone. The body is gone, so `title` comes from the newest snapshot that still had one — what the article was called when it went. `restore_rev` is the revision a restore would re-apply, and is null once pruning has aged out every body: then there is nothing left to bring back.

SuggestionList.description: Ranked nearest-scope-first (same collection, then same database, then the rest) and capped, because this answers a keystroke.

NamespaceDeleted.description: `purged` is how many tombstones went with it. `database_removed` is true when this was the last collection: MongoDB drops a database with its last collection, so that is also how a database goes.

VersionList.description: Retained snapshots, newest first. Capped by `VERSIONS_KEEP`; older ones are pruned. A deleted document still answers here — which is what makes it recoverable.

Snapshot.description: One retained version, body included. `document` is null for a deletion.

FieldDiff.description: One field's fate between two versions. `old`/`new` are absent when the field did not exist on that side.

CollaboratorList.description: Everyone granted access at exactly this scope, including the owner. `custom` describes a grant whose permissions match no named role.

CollaboratorResult.description: `doc_id` is null when the grant is on the whole collection.

Contacts.description: The caller's saved collaborator roster, which drives the sharing pickers.
